# Untzel: full reference

> Untzel is a music instrument in the browser by Techno Inspire: you tap to play a loop, then change it by touch or by editing a small text language that is analyzed, never executed.

## Start here

Untzel is a music instrument that runs in your browser. You tap once and a loop starts, picked from a template library by music style; then you change it with your fingers or by editing a short text, and the music never stops while you do.

### What Untzel is

Every sound you hear is one line of a small text language. The track tiles, the song timeline and the code editor all edit that same text, so whatever you build by touch you can read as code, and whatever you write as code shows up as tiles.

The sound is made on your device: a sound engine written in Rust runs as WebAssembly inside the browser's audio thread, and the light on the stage follows the same events the engine plays. Nothing is streamed and you need no account.

The text is analyzed, never executed. There is no JavaScript inside it, no functions and no imports, so it is safe to paste text that someone else wrote, or that an assistant wrote for you ([Using AI](https://untzel.com/docs/en/ai/)).

### Tap to play

Open [app.untzel.com](https://app.untzel.com/) and tap **Tap to play**. Browsers only allow sound after a gesture, so that first tap is what starts the audio. The music starts on the next bar, in loop mode.

This is the text the app plays first, exactly as this build ships it:

```untzel
// template: Midnight Bloom
// order: 1
// default: true
title "Midnight Bloom"
tempo 124
key a minor

kick:   kick       boom    x... x... x... x... | gain 0.9
sub:    sub        warm    a1 . . . a1 . . . / f1 . . . f1 . . . / d1 . . . d1 . . . / e1 . . . e1 . . .   | duck 0.6
bass:   bass       rolling . a2 a2 a2 . a2 c3 a2 / . f2 f2 f2 . f2 a2 f2 / . d2 d2 d2 . d2 f2 d2 / . e2 e2 e2 . g2 e2 b2   | duck 0.5 | comp 0.3 | pan 0.1 | gain 1.48
hat:    hat        tight   . x x?0.6 x . x x?0.6 x . x x?0.6 x . x x?0.7 x     | gain 0.6 | swing 0.1 | pan -0.15
ohat:   hat        open    ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x. | pan 0.15 | gain 0.85
shaker: shaker     bright  x x?0.7 x x?0.8 x x?0.7 x x?0.8 x x?0.7 x x?0.8 x x?0.7 X x?0.8   | swing 0.16 | gain 0.34 | pan 0.3
conga:  conga      open    . . x . x . . x . . x . x . x?0.4 x?0.5               | swing 0.16 | pan -0.35 | reverb room | gain 0.75
rim:    rim        click   .... ..x. .... .x.x                                   | pan 0.4 | delay 3/16 | gain 1
perc:   perc       ping    .... .... ..x. .x..                                   | pan -0.2 | delay 1/8 | reverb room
clap:   clap       tight   .... x... .... x...                                   | reverb room | gain 1
pad:    pad        noir    Am9 ~ ~ ~ / Fmaj9 ~ ~ ~ / Dm9 ~ ~ ~ / Em7 ~ ~ ~       | voicing spread | brightness sine(16) 0.3..0.7 | duck 0.5 | reverb hall | gain 0.48
pluck:  pluck      muted   Am9 ~ ~ ~ / Fmaj9 ~ ~ ~ / Dm9 ~ ~ ~ / Em7 ~ ~ ~       | arp updown | arp-rate 1/16 | arp-octaves 2 | highpass 300 | delay 3/16 | gain 0.6
keys:   epiano     soft    . Am7 . . Am7 . . . / . Fmaj7 . . Fmaj7 . . . / . Dm7 . . Dm7 . . . / . Em7 . . Em7! . . .   | voicing open | chorus 0.25 | reverb wide | gain 0.5
lead:   lead       noir    e4 ~ ~ . c4 ~ d4 ~ / a3 ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ . . / c4 ~ ~ . d4 ~ e4 ~ / g4 ~ ~ ~ e4 ~ ~ .   | legato | glide 0.08 | delay 1/4 | reverb plate | gain 0.53
answer: square     hollow  . . e5 . . . c5 . / . . a4 . . . . . / . . d5 . . . f5 . / . . e5 . . . b4 .   | delay 3/16 | reverb hall | pan -0.25 | gain 0.4
choir:  choir      monk    Am ~ ~ ~ / F ~ ~ ~ / Dm ~ ~ ~ / Em ~ ~ ~              | vowel sine(8) 0.2..0.6 | eq-high 3 | reverb hall | gain 0.5
rise:   noise      white   x~~~ ~~~~ ~~~~ ~~~~                                   | cutoff saw(8) 300..9000 | gain saw(8) 0.15..0.5
riser:  riser      noise   x... / .... / .... / .... / .... / .... / .... / ....   | length 15.5 | gain 0.6
down:   downlifter noise   x~~~ ~~~~ ~~~~ ~~~~ / .... / .... / .... / .... / .... / .... / ....   | reverb wide | gain 0.8
impact: impact     deep    x... / .... / .... / .... / .... / .... / .... / ....   | reverb sea | gain 0.9

section intro   kick hat shaker conga rim pad
section groove  kick sub bass hat ohat shaker conga rim perc clap pad keys | loop
section build   kick sub hat ohat shaker conga perc clap pad pluck rise
section break   pad pluck keys choir down
section lift    hat pad pluck choir riser
section drop    kick sub bass hat ohat shaker conga rim perc clap pad pluck lead answer choir impact
section groove2 kick sub bass hat ohat shaker conga rim perc clap keys pluck
section break2  pad keys choir lead down
section drop2   kick sub bass hat ohat shaker conga rim perc clap pad pluck keys lead answer choir impact
section outro   kick hat shaker conga rim pad

song intro 16, groove 32, build 8, break 16, lift 8, drop 32, groove2 16, break2 16, lift 8, drop2 32, outro 16
```

### Your first loop in 2 minutes

1. Tap **Code**, next to **Drop**. On a phone the code opens as a sheet; on a computer it opens in the side panel.
2. Select all of the text and replace it with this:

```untzel
// my first loop
tempo 124
key a minor

kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.   | swing 0.1
bass: bass a1 . . a1 . . e2 .    | cutoff 500
```

3. Stop typing. On the next bar the new text plays.
4. Change one number, for example `cutoff 500` to `cutoff 1200`. A change to a plain number sounds right away; a change to a pattern waits for the next bar.
5. Break something on purpose: delete a letter of `kick`. The line gets an error mark with a message, and the previous version keeps playing. Invalid code never stops the music.

### Where to go next

- [Using the app](https://untzel.com/docs/en/app/): every screen, gesture and keyboard shortcut.
- [Language guide](https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/): the language, one idea at a time, each with an example you can paste.
- [Cookbook](https://untzel.com/docs/en/cookbook/): grooves, builds and a whole song with the instruments that exist today.
- [Using AI](https://untzel.com/docs/en/ai/): a ready prompt that teaches an assistant to write Untzel for you.

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/

## Using the app

Untzel is one page: tracks, song, code and track details open as tabs and sheets over the stage, so moving around never interrupts the sound. The labels below are the ones the app shows in the language of this page.

### The screen

- **Top bar**, over the stage: the Untzel logo, linked to untzel.com, a divider and the title of the song ([Projects and the song title](#projects)). On a computer **Saved** next to the title says the project is stored on this device. At the right, **Export** and **Menu** ([The menu](#menu)). Export stays inactive until the first tap: it acts on the music that plays.
- **Stage**: the light. It reacts to the notes as they play and is decorative for screen readers.
- **Transport**: play and stop, tempo, key, the mode and the position. Then the button that hides the controls, **Code** and **Drop**. On a computer the transport is one line with the `Loop` / `Song` switch. Under it, in both modes, the play range and its ruler ([Play range](#play-range)); in Loop mode the **Length** chip sits next to them ([Loop length](#loop-length)). The CPU meter is in the transport from 1024 px wide; on a narrower screen it moves to the footer of the instrument library.
- **Tracks**: a grid of tiles on a phone, a table on a computer.
- **Song**: the parts of the song as a list, in the order they play. A tab on a phone; on a computer, next to the tracks in Song mode.
- **Code**: the text itself.
- **Footer**: the line "Powered by Untzel · Techno Inspire", across the whole width and always on screen. Nothing the app opens covers it.

### Waiting screen and templates

Before the first tap the stage shows a slow haze and the **Tap to play** button. Below it, **Start from a template** shows the template library: the **Style** list, with every music style in alphabetical order and the number of projects of each, and below it the projects of the open style as cards with their name, tempo and key, read from the text itself. On the keyboard, type the first letters of a style to jump to it. Tap a card, then **Tap to play**, and that project plays; everything in a template can be changed: add tracks, edit every step and sound, build a whole song. With no choice, the first tap plays the template marked as the first one.

When this device already has a project, the waiting screen also offers **Continue** followed by the title of the project you edited last, which opens it ([Projects and the song title](#projects)).

The **Blank** card comes before the style list. Pick it and the button becomes **Start from scratch**: it turns the sound on and opens an empty project without playing. With no track, the tracks area says **Start with a sound** and offers **Add track** and four starters (kick, bass, hats, chords): each one enters with a ready pattern, in the key of the project, and starts the music.

The library of this build, generated from its template folder. The project names are names, not copy, so they read the same in every language:

| Style | Template | Tempo | Key | Tracks | Song |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Melodic techno | Midnight Bloom | 124 | a minor | 20 | 200 bars |
| Melodic techno | Night Petals | 122 | d minor | 20 | 216 bars |
| Melodic techno | After Hours | 122 | c minor | 20 | 184 bars |
| Afro house | Red Earth | 121 | e dorian | 22 | 208 bars |
| Indie dance | Coastline | 118 | eb major | 27 | 168 bars |
| House | Sunday Piano | 125 | f major | 17 | 176 bars |
| House | Disco Lights | 118 | g major | 19 | 176 bars |
| House | Golden Hour | 121 | eb major | 19 | 176 bars |
| Psytrance | Full Moon | 145 | f# phrygian | 16 | 232 bars |
| Trance | Eternal Horizon | 138 | d minor | 20 | 224 bars |
| Deep house | Night Garden | 115 | d dorian | 7 | loop only |
| Downtempo | Blue Lounge | 96 | g minor | 9 | loop only |
| Acid techno | Warehouse | 138 | f minor | 14 | 144 bars |
| Tech house | Low Ceiling | 126 | g minor | 14 | 176 bars |
| Amapiano | Velvet Rooftop | 113 | f minor | 20 | 176 bars |
| Hip hop | Crate Digger | 90 | d minor | 14 | 96 bars |
| outside the styles | Blank | 124 | a minor | 0 | loop only |

Available now: Template library by style. A Style list on the waiting screen, in alphabetical order with the number of projects of each; every project can be changed completely.

Available now: Continue where you left off. Continue on the waiting screen opens the project you edited last on this device.

### The menu

**Menu**, at the right of the top bar, opens one menu for the whole app: a sheet on a phone, a panel under the button on a computer. The arrow keys walk every item in reading order, `Home` and `End` go to the ends, a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it, and `Esc` closes the menu and returns focus to the button. The groups, in this order:

- **Project**: **New project…** (blank or from a template), **Open project…**, **Rename song**, **Duplicate**, **Save file**, **Open file…** and **Delete project**, which you can undo for 10 seconds. With no project open, only the items that do not need one are there.
- **Share and export**: **Share link…** and **Export video or audio…** ([Share and Export](#share-export)). The group appears only with a project open. Like **Export**, both stay inactive until the first tap, and their hint says why.
- **Settings**: **Language**, with Português and English, changes every label at once without reloading; the choice is saved on this device. **Preview sounds** plays the notes while you edit them. **Reduced motion** follows the system until you change it here, and then says it is set on this device. The switches and the language keep the menu open.
- **Help**: **Documentation**, which opens these pages in a new tab, **Keyboard shortcuts** and **About and licence**.

These docs and the app live on different addresses, so the language picked on these pages does not carry over to the app: pick it in the app's menu.

### Projects and the song title

Every project has a title. The title is the `title` line of the text ([Language guide](https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/#title)): the top bar shows it, the browser tab reads `<title> · Untzel`, and it names the files you save and export. Tap the title in the top bar, or choose **Rename song** in the menu, to rename the song: `Enter` or leaving the field renames, `Esc` gives up. A new project is called **Untitled**, a template keeps the template's name, a received link opens as **Remix of** followed by its title, and a duplicate adds **(copy)**.

Projects are saved in this browser, on this device, and never leave it. A project is stored one second after your first edit, and again one second after each later one; a template you only played creates nothing. `Mod+S` saves at once, without a dialog. **Open project…** lists the projects of this device, the one edited last first, each with when it was edited, its tempo and how many tracks it has; its buttons rename, duplicate, save as a file or delete it, and a search appears above eight projects. Opening, creating, duplicating or deleting a project stops the music cleanly and goes back to the waiting screen; nothing you were editing is lost on the way.

Clearing the browser's data deletes the projects: **Save file** keeps a copy. Where the browser refuses to store anything (a private window, a full disk), the app says so and the open project keeps playing; it is just not saved.

Available now: Projects on this device and the project menu. Every project saved in this browser one second after an edit, with open, rename, duplicate and delete with undo, all from one menu.

Available now: Song title. The title line names the song in the top bar, the browser tab, the files and the exported video.

### Tracks

Each track is a tile with its name, its instrument, a 16-step preview and an adjust button.

| Gesture on a tile | What happens | When |
|---|---|---|
| tap | turns the track on or off | on the next bar; a ring fills until then |
| drag up or down | moves the track's `tone` | immediately |
| hold | solo while you hold | immediately |
| adjust button | opens the track detail | |

On a computer the table shows the name, the pattern, `M` (mute), `S` (solo) and `tone` for every track.

Every name the app shows can be edited where it appears: a track in the head of its detail, or with a double-click and the pencil in the table; a part in the pencil of its row and in the head of its editor. Lowercase letters, numbers, `-` or `_`, starting with a letter, up to 24 characters; the words of the language are not names. `Enter` or leaving the field renames, `Esc` or **Cancel** gives up, and a wrong name is explained under the field and never written. Renaming a track also renames it in every `section`; renaming a part renames it in the `song`. One edit, one undo step, and the music keeps playing.

### Adding a track

The last tile is always **Add track**. It opens the instrument library: a search over names, model names, sounds, descriptions and tags, the chips **All** and nine categories (Drums, Bass, Keys, Plucks, Pads, Brass, Leads, Voices, FX), and the instruments grouped, each with its model name, how many tracks already use it, its description and its number of sounds. A group shows three instruments until you ask for all of them.

The play button of a row previews the instrument in the key of your music while the music keeps playing; its sounds appear as chips, and tapping one switches the preview. The add button adds the instrument with the sound you are hearing. The new track gets the next free name (`hat2`, `bass3`), the instrument's default pattern, and starts on the next bar; the sheet closes and the new track's detail opens. You can pick the same instrument as many times as you like: each track is its own instance. When nothing matches, the sheet suggests up to three close names.

`piano`, `strings`, `harp`, `mallet`, `bell`, `kalimba` and `choir` play recordings, and so do the `ooh` and `aah` sounds of `vox` ([Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/), [Credits](https://untzel.com/docs/en/credits/)). A recording is downloaded only when a track uses it; until it arrives, the instrument plays its synthesized voice, so the music never waits.

Available now: Recorded voices for vox and choir. The ooh and aah sounds of vox and choir play recorded singers from VocalSet (CC BY 4.0), loaded only when a track uses them.

Available now: Recorded piano, strings, harp, mallet, bell and kalimba. Recordings from Salamander Grand Piano (CC BY 3.0), VSCO 2 Community Edition and the Versilian Community Sample Library (CC0), downloaded only when a track uses them.

Available now: Instrument library with search and preview. Nine categories, from drums to FX; search, preview a sound before adding it, and add the same instrument as often as you like.

### Track detail

The detail shows everything about one track: solo and mute, the length of its pattern, the steps per bar, the bars of the pattern, the step grid, its sound, its effects and its mix. **Duplicate** and **Delete** sit at the bottom.

- The **Pattern** chip picks how many bars the pattern has; new bars repeat the last one. **Steps per bar**, `8 · 16 · 32`, rewrites every bar of the track; the steps that exist keep their place in time.
- The bar thumbnails show the steps of each bar; the one you edit has an orange outline and the one playing a white mark. The arrows, or a swipe on the grid, change the bar you edit, and **Copy bar**, **Paste here** and **Clear bar** act on it.
- On a drum, tapping a step turns it on or off. On an instrument with notes, tapping a step selects it and opens the note picker: any note of the instrument's range, a hold or a rest, chords on a chord instrument, and **Scale lock**, which keeps the step in the scale of your music. With **Preview sounds** on, here or in the menu, the notes play as you edit them.
- **Sound**: the sound picker lists the instrument's sounds with their descriptions, and below it one control for every parameter of the instrument ([Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/)).
- **Effects · play in this order**: the insert effects in chain order, each with its controls and a ×; **Add effect** adds one at the end of the chain.
- **Patterns**, under solo and mute: the instrument's ready patterns as chips, the current one marked. A tap previews the pattern in the track itself, from the next bar for 16 bars, without changing the text; a second tap, or **Use**, writes it. The patterns enter already in the key of your music.
- **Change sound**, next to **Sound**, swaps the instrument and keeps the pattern: the library opens listing only the instruments that can play it, and says what is kept and what is dropped.
- **Tone** is one knob over several parameters. When the text writes one of them (`open`, `cutoff`), that parameter wins: the knob says who sets it and **Use Tone** takes the written parameter out, with an Undo.
- **Mix**: `gain` is a fader in dB, from Off through −60 dB to +6 dB, with 0 dB at three quarters of the travel; a double tap returns to 0 dB. The text keeps `gain` as a plain number (`gain 1` is 0 dB). Then `pan`, `reverb` and `duck`.

Every change here becomes a small edit of the text, which you can undo.

### Transport and Drop

**Drop**, in loop mode, turns every muted track on in one edit, on the next bar. In song mode it stays in place but does nothing.

The tempo and the key in the transport are buttons. The tempo opens `−`, a field and `+` from 40 to 300 BPM, and **Tap tempo** (four taps, or `T` on a keyboard). The key opens the twelve tonics and the scales `minor`, `major`, `dorian`, `phrygian` and `chromatic`; notes outside the new scale move to the nearest note in it. The key is written in lowercase, as in the text (`a minor`), in every language. Both enter on the next bar. In Song mode, when the part playing has its own `| tempo`, the button shows the tempo that sounds and the editor, **Song tempo**, still edits the `tempo` line.

**Undo** and **Redo** sit in the transport on a phone and in the head of the Code panel on a computer, and say what they took back. On a keyboard, `Ctrl+Z` and `Ctrl+Shift+Z` (`Command` on a Mac).

The CPU meter shows how much of the device the music uses. The language has no limit on tracks; the device does, and the meter is how you see it. From 1024 px wide it sits in the transport; on a narrower screen it is in the footer of the instrument library, and above 80% the library warns that the device is near its limit.

### Loop length

In Loop mode the transport has the **Length** chip. It opens the length choice, 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bars; a tap picks one and closes it, and `[` and `]` step through the same lengths on a keyboard. The chip writes `loop <bars>` in the text ([Language guide](https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/#loop-length)) and the new length enters on the next bar, without stopping the music. Any other length, up to 16, is written in the Code panel, and the chip then shows it as written. The chip is hidden in Song mode, where the song decides the length.

Available now: Loop length in bars. loop <bars> sets how many bars one pass of loop mode lasts; the Length chip of the transport writes it.

### Play range

Under the transport a ruler shows the loop, one segment per bar, or the song, one block per part, with the bar that is playing lit. On it you choose the play range: the stretch that repeats while you work, from one bar up to all of them.

- Drag one of the two handles, or tap a first bar and then a last one. The row above the ruler says what is chosen, `Range: bars 3–6`; its × (`Clear range`) goes back to the whole loop or song.
- On a keyboard, a focused handle moves one bar with the arrows and four with `Shift` or `PageUp` and `PageDown`; `Home` and `End` go to the ends.
- The position follows the range: `Loop · bars 3–6 of 8 · bar 4`.
- The range enters on the next bar and the music never stops. Outside the new range, the music jumps to its start at that bar; inside it, it goes on without a jump.

In Loop mode the range always repeats. In Song mode the row has a **Cycle** switch: on, the range repeats; off, the music starts there and plays on into the rest of the song.

The range is how you play, not what the music is, like play, stop and the mode. It is never written into the text, so undo does not undo it, and for now it is not kept in the link or the file either: it lasts while the app is open. Each mode keeps its own.

Available now: Play range in Loop and Song. Choose the bars or parts that repeat, play one part alone, and export the same range. Never written into the text.

### Loop and Song

In **Loop** mode every track without `mute` plays forever. In **Song** mode the sections play in the order of the `song` line ([Language guide](https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/#sections)). Switching modes while playing takes effect on the next 4-bar phrase, and entering Song starts from the first part.

In Song mode the parts of the song are a list, in the order they play: each with its name, its length and how many tracks it has; the one playing fills as it goes. Each row has its own play button, `Play <part> only`: it sets the range to that part with **Cycle** on, and the part plays alone, round and round, from the next bar; a second tap while the music plays clears the range. The bracket button of a row sets the range to start at that part, and **To here** extends it to another one.

Open a part to choose its tracks, its length, **Play from here**, **Duplicate** and **Move**. **Play from here** moves the start of the range to that part, or, with no range, plays the song from there, on the next bar. **Add part from what is playing** writes a new section with the tracks that sound and adds it to the end of the song. That is how you build and play a finished song live.

### The Code panel

**Code**, next to **Drop**, opens the text. Tap it again to close it. While the music plays, the words that are sounding light up in orange.

- When you stop typing, the text is analyzed. If it is valid, it plays from the next bar; a line under the editor shows how long until then.
- If it is invalid, the wrong part is underlined, the message appears in the language of the app with its stable English code, and the previous version keeps playing. Nothing stops.
- When a gesture changes the text, the changed line is highlighted for a moment.

The editor reads the text as the Untzel language: keywords, instruments, notes, numbers and comments each have their colour, and every track line carries the colour of its track in the margin, the same colour as its light on the stage and its dot in the tracks. On a phone a long line only wraps before a `|`, so a modifier never sits alone. On a computer the panel's left edge is a divider: drag it, or focus it and use the arrows, to make the panel wider; a double-click returns to the default width.

- **Completion.** `Ctrl+Space` lists what fits where the cursor is: instruments and statements at the start of a line, notes and chords of your key in a pattern, parameters after `|`, signals with the parameter's whole range, tonics and scales after `key`, tracks after `section`, sections after `song`. The arrows choose, `Enter` or `Tab` accept, `Esc` closes.
- **Help under the cursor.** Resting on a word, or `Alt+I` on a keyboard, shows what it is: a parameter with its range, default and unit, an instrument with its group and parameters, a signal with its shape and period.
- **Quick fixes.** An error with a known fix shows a button under the message, for example `Change to kick` for `kik`, next to **Ignore**. `Mod+.` applies the fix under the cursor, or the first one of the text. A fix touches only the part it names, and the music keeps playing.
- `Esc` says how to leave: right after it, `Tab` moves out of the editor, and `Esc` again closes the panel.

Available now: Commands under the code. A command line in the Code panel that makes the same minimal edits as the controls, with a preview before anything destructive.

Under the code, the **Commands** button opens a command line, closed by default. Each command makes the same minimal edit as the controls do, through the same text: it is read, never executed, and the music never stops. A change that removes something, or touches more than one line, first shows a preview of the lines that change with **Apply** and **Cancel**; nothing changes until you apply. While the music plays, a change enters on the next bar and the line says so, then says from which bar it plays.

- `Enter` runs the line. `Tab` completes with the chosen suggestion, `Alt+↓` and `Alt+↑` choose another, `↑` and `↓` walk the history. `Esc` closes the suggestions or cancels a preview, and `Mod+Enter` applies it.
- A command with a typo answers with the closest one: `mute kik` offers `mute kick` as a chip, and a tap writes it on the line.
- `help` lists the commands, `help <command>` explains one, and `explain` says in plain words what a line or a track does. Results and help read in the language of the app; the commands themselves are words of the language and stay as written.
- The divider between the code and the commands moves with a drag or, focused, with the arrows.

| Command | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `help [command]` | list the commands, or explain one | `help set` |
| `add <instrument> [name]` | a new track | `add bass` |
| `duplicate <track>` | copy a track under the next free name | `duplicate bass` |
| `remove <track>` | delete a track and its name in the sections | `remove ride` |
| `rename <track> <new>` | rename a track and the sections that use it | `rename bass acid` |
| `mute <track>` | turn a track off on the next bar | `mute hat` |
| `unmute <track>` | turn a track on on the next bar | `unmute hat` |
| `solo <track>` | hear one track alone; again to release | `solo bass` |
| `tempo <bpm>` | 40 to 300 | `tempo 124` |
| `key <tonic> <scale>` | the key notes snap to | `key a minor` |
| `loop <bars>` | bars of one pass in loop mode, 1 to 16 | `loop 8` |
| `set <track> <param> <value>` | a number, or a signal with its range | `set bass cutoff sine(8) 300..2400` |
| `tone <track> <value>` | the track's tone, 0 to 1 | `tone bass 0.7` |
| `steps <track> <8\|16\|32>` | steps per bar | `steps hat 32` |
| `bars <track> <n>` | bars of the pattern, 1 to 16 | `bars bass 4` |
| `section <name> <tracks…>` | create a section or change its tracks | `section drop kick hat bass` |
| `song <part bars, …>` | write the song | `song intro 8, drop 16` |
| `play` | start the music | `play` |
| `stop` | stop the music | `stop` |
| `drop` | turn every track on, in loop mode | `drop` |
| `fix` | apply every safe quick fix | `fix` |
| `explain <line\|track>` | what a line or a track does, in plain words | `explain bass` |
| `undo` | undo the last change | `undo` |
| `redo` | redo what was undone | `redo` |
| `clear` | clear the results | `clear` |

### Hide the controls

The round button in the transport hides everything under it, so the stage fills the screen; `H` does the same on a keyboard. The transport stays with play, the position, **Code** and **Drop**; the top bar and the footer with the attribution stay as they are. The choice is saved on the device and the music never stops while you switch.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Space` | Play or stop | outside the code editor |
| `1–9` | Turn one of the first nine tracks on or off | outside the code editor |
| `A` | Add a track | outside the code editor |
| `D` | Drop, in loop mode | outside the code editor |
| `H` | Hide or show the controls; the stage fills the screen | outside the code editor |
| `[ ]` | The previous or next loop length (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 bars), in loop mode | outside the code editor |
| `Esc` | Close the open sheet and return focus; from the code editor, press it twice | anywhere, also in the editor |
| `Mod+Z` | Undo | anywhere, also in the editor |
| `Mod+Shift+Z` | Redo | anywhere, also in the editor |
| `Mod+Enter` | Apply the text now, on the next bar, without waiting | anywhere, also in the editor |
| `Mod+.` | Stop | outside the code editor |
| `Mod+S` | Save the project on this device now, without a dialog | anywhere, also in the editor |

Mod is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.

### When a change plays

A change to a plain number, such as `gain 0.6` to `gain 0.4`, sounds immediately. Everything else waits for the next bar: patterns, tracks, `mute`, signals, tempo, key, sections and the song. That is why the music never jumps.

A pattern can be up to 64 bars long, the loop from 1 to 16 bars, and a part of the song from 1 to 256 bars.

### Sheets

Every sheet and the side panel close with the × button and with `Esc`, and focus returns to the control that opened them. On a phone, a sheet with a handle also closes when you drag it down.

### Share and Export

**Share link…**, in the menu, opens the share sheet, which sends your music as a link; when the song is too long for a link, it offers a `.untzel` file instead. **Save file** and **Open file…**, in the menu, save and open a `.untzel` file at any time, and a file dropped on the stage opens too.

**Export**, in the top bar, opens the export sheet. Opening it renders nothing: you choose first, then press **Render**.

- **Format**: **Story** 9:16, **Video** 16:9 or **Audio** WAV, each with the length the file will have, closing card included.
- **Range**: with a play range, **Selected range** is chosen. It starts as a copy of the play range on the same ruler as the transport, and its two handles move by steps (1/16 of a note; **Fine**, Shift or Alt for 1/64), so a video can start and end on any step. The start and the end show as time and bar.beat. The Story takes up to 1:00, video and audio up to 10:00, 4K up to 4:21; a handle stops at the limit and the line under the ruler says why. Editing it never changes what plays, and **Use play range** returns to the copy. **Listen**, next to **Fine**, plays the range from its first bar and stops after its last; pressed again, as **Stop**, it stops at once. The play range stays as it was, the export ruler shows the bar that sounds, and closing the sheet does not stop the music. Without a play range, the Story starts on **Now playing**, about 15 seconds from the bar that sounds, and video and audio on the loop or the song, with **Selected range** one tap away. In the song, **From** and **To** pick the parts, and in the loop, **Bars** picks 8, 16, 32 or 64 bars.
- **Quality**, for video: **HD** and **4K**, each with its resolution, HD chosen. Render checks this device first. If it cannot take 4K, it renders HD. After that test, 4K shows only on a device that can render it in time, with about how long the render takes.
- The preview shows what the file will contain: the light in the format's shape, the Techno Inspire | Untzel logo and the address untzel.com, apart from the logo, on every frame, the song's title on a card for the first 1.5 seconds and then as a caption, and the 2-second closing card with only the logo and the address.

Videos are MP4 files with H.264 video and AAC sound, 12 Mbit/s in HD and 30 Mbit/s in 4K; where the browser cannot encode AAC the sound is Opus, and the line that says the file is ready adds **Opus audio**. The song's title names the file and goes into its metadata, in MP4 and in WAV. On a device that cannot encode H.264, Story and Video are inactive and the sheet suggests the WAV export or another browser. When the video encoder does not answer in time, the sheet says so and shows **Try again**, which starts the same render again.

While it renders, the sheet shows the progress and the time left, with **Cancel**, and the music keeps playing. When it is done the preview becomes the file itself, and **Download** saves it; where the system accepts files, **Share** sends it. The logo and the closing card are a condition of the license and have no option to remove them.

Available now: Share as a link. The whole text in the link fragment; a file when it is too long.

Available now: Export: story, video and WAV. Rendered offline: a 9:16 story up to 1:00 (about 15 s of what is playing without a play range), a 16:9 video or WAV audio up to 10:00, from the play range, the loop or the song. The music keeps playing.

Available now: Export in HD or 4K. HD and 4K from the first time the sheet opens; Render tests the device first and renders HD where it cannot take 4K. After that test, 4K shows only where it passed.

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/app/

## Language guide

Untzel code is a small, closed language for music. It is analyzed, never executed: there are no functions, variables, loops or imports, so the same text always plays the same music, in the app and anywhere else it is opened. Keywords, instrument names, parameters and error codes are in English; the app shows each error message in its own language.

Every example on this page plays as it is. Copy it, paste it into the Code panel and change it.

### The structure of a text

A text has four parts, in this order, and every part is optional:

1. globals: `title`, `tempo`, `key`, `swing` and `loop`;
2. tracks, one per line;
3. sections, with `section`;
4. at most one `song`.

Empty lines are ignored and `//` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.

```untzel
// globals first, then tracks, then sections, then the song
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.08

kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
bass: bass a1 . . a1 . . c2 .

section intro kick hat
section main  kick hat bass

song intro 8, main 16 | loop
```

Without a `song`, every track that is not muted plays in a loop.

### Tempo, key, swing and loop

`tempo` sets the beats per minute, from 40 to 300; without it the text plays at 132. A value outside the range is an error, never a silent correction.

`key` takes a tonic, `a` to `g` with an optional `b` or `#`, and a scale: `minor`, `major`, `dorian`, `phrygian` or `chromatic`. Without it the key is `c minor`.

`swing` delays the even eighths, from 0 up to 0.5. Each global can appear once.

```untzel
tempo 126
key d dorian
swing 0.12

hat:  hat  x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.
bass: bass d2 . f2 . a2 . c3 .
```

#### Loop length

`loop` sets how many bars one pass of Loop mode lasts, a whole number from 1 to 16. On every pass all patterns and signals start again from bar 1: a 2-bar pattern plays 4 times in `loop 8`, and a pattern longer than the loop plays only its first bars. Without `loop`, every pattern repeats on its own length, as before.

```untzel
// 8 bars per pass: the 2-bar bass plays 4 times and the cutoff rises across the pass
tempo 124
key c minor
loop 8
kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
bass: bass . c2 . c2 . c2 . eb2 / . ab1 . ab1 . c2 . g1 | cutoff saw(8) 300..2400
```

A new length enters on the next bar and the music never stops. Song mode ignores `loop`: there the sections and the `song` line decide. `loop` is still a valid track name and the word at the end of `song … | loop`. The **Length** chip of the transport writes this line for you ([Using the app](https://untzel.com/docs/en/app/#loop-length)).

#### Song title
`title "Midnight Coast"` names the song: up to 60 characters between double quotes, where `\"` writes a quote and `\\` a backslash. It never changes the sound. The app shows it in the top bar and in the browser tab, and it goes into the file names, the exported video and the shared link. Renaming the song in the app writes this line ([Using the app](https://untzel.com/docs/en/app/#projects)). An empty title or one longer than 60 characters is a warning, not an error: the music keeps playing, without a title or with its first 60 characters. A second `title` line is an error, like a second `tempo`. `title` is still a valid track name.

```untzel
// the title names the song; it never changes the sound
title "Midnight Coast"
tempo 122
key f minor
kick: kick  x... x... x... x...
keys: piano Fm7 ~ ~ ~ / Dbmaj7 ~ ~ ~
```

### Tracks with names

A track line is an optional name and a colon, an instrument, a pattern, and modifiers after `|`. The name is how sections, tiles and messages refer to the track. Names are lower case, start with a letter, and have at most 24 characters.

Two tracks can use the same instrument with different patterns and sounds: each track is an independent instance. A track without a name takes the instrument's name, or the next free number.

```untzel
// two bass tracks: two independent instances
sub:  bass c1 . . . c1 . . .   | cutoff 160
bass: bass . . c2 . . . eb2 .  | cutoff 900 | pan 0.2

// without a name, a track takes the instrument's: hat, then hat2
hat ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
hat x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.        | gain 0.4
```

The order of the lines is the order of the tracks on screen.

### Patterns: the mini-notation

A pattern describes one bar; `/` separates the bars of a longer pattern, which repeats when it ends. The steps of a bar divide it equally.

| Write | Means |
|---|---|
| `x` `X` `.` | a hit, an accented hit, a rest. In a run like `x...` every character is a step |
| `~` | holds the previous step one step longer: `x~~~` holds a hit for four steps |
| `c2` `eb2` `f#1` | a note with its octave, for instruments that play notes |
| `[x x]` | a group: subdivides one step |
| `x?` `x?0.3` | plays with a chance; without a number the chance is 0.5 |
| `x*4` `[c2 g1]*2` | repeats inside the same step |
| `/` | the next bar of the pattern |

```untzel
kick:  kick X... x... X... x...
clap:  hat  .... x~.. .... x~..   | open 0.4
roll:  hat  x x [x x] x*2         | decay 0.03
ghost: hat  x?0.3 x? x? x?        | gain 0.5
fill:  kick x... x... x... x... / x... x... x.x. xxxx
```

#### Counting steps

Spaces separate elements, but in a run of hits each character is already a step, so `x... x...` and `x...x...` are the same eight steps. `x... x... x... x...` is a bar of 16 steps, each a sixteenth; `c2 . eb2 c3 . c2 g1 .` is 8 steps, each an eighth. A bar has at most 64 steps and groups nest at most 4 deep.

### Notes and chords

Instruments that play notes take lower-case note names with an octave: `c1`, `eb2`, `f#1`. A `.` is a rest and `~` holds the note.

```untzel
key c minor

sub:  bass c1 ~ . c1 ~ . c1 .         | cutoff 180
line: bass c2 eb2 g2 bb2 c3 . g2 .    | cutoff 1200 | decay 0.2
```

Notes joined by `+` sound together in one step, as a stack you voice yourself: `c3+eb3+g3`. A `!` after a hit or a note accents it, like `X` on a drum.

```untzel
key c minor
keys: piano c3+eb3+g3 ~ ~ . bb2+d3+f3 ~ . . | reverb wide
kick: kick x . . . x . . . x . . . x! . x .
lead: lead c4! . eb4 . g4 . bb4! .      | cutoff 2000
```

Chord names start with a capital letter, as in `Cm7`, `Abmaj7` or `Gsus4`, and need an instrument of kind chord. Writing a chord for an instrument that plays notes is the error `PATTERN_KIND_MISMATCH` ([reference](https://untzel.com/docs/en/reference/#error-pattern-kind-mismatch)).

Available now: Chords. Chord names such as Cm7 need an instrument of kind chord.

### The scale lock

With a key, every note outside the scale moves to the nearest degree of it, so a wrong note is impossible. `| free` turns the lock off for one track, and `key c chromatic` turns it off for the whole text.

```untzel
key c minor

// in c minor, e2 plays eb2 and b2 plays bb2
locked: bass c2 e2 g2 b2
// free plays every note as written
loose:  bass c2 e2 g2 b2   | free
```

### Modifiers

Modifiers come after the pattern, each after a `|`, and are read from left to right. If the same modifier appears twice, the last one wins and the earlier one gets the warning `DUPLICATE_MODIFIER`; a warning never stops the music.

There are general modifiers every track accepts (`gain`, `pan`, `tone`, `reverb`, `delay`, `duck`, `transpose`, `swing`, `shift`, `mute`, `free`) and the parameters of each instrument, such as `cutoff` on `bass` or `open` on `hat`. The full table with every range is in the [reference](https://untzel.com/docs/en/reference/#general-modifiers), and every instrument parameter is on the [Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/) page.

```untzel
kick: kick x... x... x... x...       | drive 0.4
bass: bass c2 . c2 . c2 . eb2 .      | duck 0.7 | tone 0.6
echo: bass . . g2 . . . c3 .         | delay 3/16 | reverb sea | gain 0.5 | pan -0.4
up:   bass c2 . . . c2 . . .         | transpose 12 | shift 2 | mute
```

When `tone` and a parameter it moves appear together, the explicit parameter wins.

### Signals

Any numeric parameter that allows it can take a slow wave instead of a number: a shape, a period in bars and a range. The range is required and stays inside the parameter's limits; the period is at most 256 bars.

| Shape | Moves |
|---|---|
| `sine(8)` | smoothly up and down |
| `tri(4)` | in straight lines up and down |
| `saw(4)` | up, then starts again |
| `square(2)` | between the two ends |
| `rand(1)` | to a new value every period, the same on every play |

```untzel
bass: bass c2 . c2 . c2 . eb2 .   | cutoff sine(8) 300..2400
hat:  hat  x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.    | open tri(4) 0..0.8 | pan rand(1) -0.5..0.5
rise: hat  x x x x x x x x        | gain saw(4) 0.1..0.8
gate: hat  x*4 x*4 x*4 x*4        | gain square(2) 0.2..0.6
```

In a song, a signal starts again at the start of every section, so `saw(4)` in a 4-bar section rises exactly across it ([Cookbook](https://untzel.com/docs/en/cookbook/#saw-build)).

### Sections and the song

`section` names a set of tracks that play together; a track can be in as many sections as you like. A section can change the `tempo` from its start and the `gain` of all its tracks. `song` plays sections in order, each for a number of bars, from 1 to 256; the same section can come back.

```untzel
tempo 124
key a minor

kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
sub:  bass a1 . . a1 . . a1 .     | cutoff 180
bass: bass . a2 . a2 . c3 . e2    | cutoff saw(4) 300..1800

section intro kick hat
section build kick hat sub bass   | gain 0.8
section drop  kick hat sub bass   | tempo 126

song intro 8, build 4, drop 16, intro 4
```

#### Looping the song

A song stops at its end. With `| loop` at the end of the `song` line it starts again.

```untzel
kick: kick x... x... x... x...
bass: bass c2 . . c2 . . g1 .

section a kick
section b kick bass

song a 4, b 8 | loop
```

#### Sections without a song

```untzel
kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.

// no song: in Song mode each section plays 8 bars, in order, in a cycle
section first  kick
section second kick hat
```

### Loop and Song modes

The mode is not written in the text: it is a switch of the transport, like play and stop. In Loop mode every track without `mute` plays forever, in passes of `loop <bars>` when the text has it, and sections are ignored. In Song mode the parts play in order; with sections but no song, each section plays 8 bars in order, in a cycle. `mute` silences a track in both modes, even inside a section. The play range is not written either: choosing which bars or parts repeat changes how you play, never the text ([Using the app](https://untzel.com/docs/en/app/#play-range)).

### Limits

The language has no limit on tracks, tracks per instrument, sections or song parts; the device does, and the CPU meter shows how much is in use. The fixed limits protect the analyzer and keep a text readable: a text has at most 65,536 characters, a pattern at most 64 bars. Every limit is in the [reference](https://untzel.com/docs/en/reference/#limits).

### Determinism

Chance (`?`) and `rand` are drawn from a seed made of the text itself, the track name and the bar. The same text plays the same notes every time, on every device. Change one character of the text and the draw changes; the `title` line is the exception, so renaming a song never changes what it plays.

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/

## Language reference

The complete language on one page: order, statements, values, every modifier, every limit, the grammar and every error with its message and fix. Numbers in the tables come from the analyzer of this build. The [guide](https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/) explains the same things with examples.

### Order of a text

Globals, then tracks, then sections, then the song. Each global (`title`, `tempo`, `key`, `swing`, `loop`) at most once, and at most one `song`. Text out of this order is the error `OUT_OF_ORDER`.

| Statement | Form |
|---|---|
| title | `title "<text>"`, up to 60 characters; `\"` writes a quote and `\\` a backslash |
| tempo | `tempo <bpm>` |
| key | `key <tonic> <scale>`, tonic `a` to `g` with optional `b` or `#`; scale `minor`, `major`, `dorian`, `phrygian` or `chromatic` |
| swing | `swing <amount>` |
| loop | `loop <bars>`, a whole number |
| track | `[<name>:] <instrument> <pattern> ( \| <modifier> [value] )*` |
| section | `section <name> <track> <track>... ( \| tempo <bpm> ) ( \| gain <value> )` |
| song | `song <section> <bars>, <section> <bars>... [ \| loop ]` |

Tempo goes from 40 to 300 with 132 as default; swing from 0 to 0.5; loop from 1 to 16 bars, absent by default; the default key is `c minor`.

### Names

Track and section names follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, at most 24 characters, unique among tracks and unique among sections. A track without a name takes the instrument's name, or `<instrument><n>` with the next free number from 2: explicit names are reserved first, then unnamed tracks are numbered in text order. Only repeated explicit names are the error `DUPLICATE_TRACK_NAME`.

### Pattern elements

| Element | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| hits | `x...`, `X.x~` | each character a step: hit, accent, rest, hold |
| note | `c2`, `eb2`, `f#1` | lower case, optional `b` or `#`, octave digit |
| chord | `Cm7`, `Abmaj7` | capital root, optional `b` or `#`, quality `m`, `7`, `m7`, `maj7`, `sus2`, `sus4` or `dim` (none is major) |
| rest | `.` | one silent step |
| hold | `~` | the previous element one step longer |
| group | `[x x]` | subdivides one step; nests at most 4 deep |
| chance | `x?`, `c2?0.3` | plays with that chance, 0.5 without a number |
| repeat | `x*4` | whole number from 1 to 16, inside the same step |
| bar | `/` | the next bar of the pattern |

Drum instruments play hits, pitched instruments play notes, chord instruments play chords; anything else is `PATTERN_KIND_MISMATCH`.

### General modifiers

Every track accepts these, whatever its instrument. The parameters of each instrument are on the [Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/) page.

| Modifier | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mute` | no value | silences the track |
| `free` | no value | turns the scale lock off for this track |
| `legato` | no value | one-voice instruments glide from note to note without a new attack |
| `gain` | 0 to 2, or a signal | volume |
| `pan` | -1 to 1, or a signal | position in the stereo field, left to right |
| `duck` | 0 to 1, or a signal | how much the track dips when the kick plays (sidechain) |
| `tone` | 0 to 1, or a signal | one-finger timbre macro: moves the parameters the instrument maps to it |
| `reverb` | small, wide, sea, room, plate, hall, and dub, or 0 to 1 | send to a reverb space by name (send 0.3), or a send amount to wide |
| `transpose` | whole number, -24 to 24 | semitones, still under the scale lock |
| `swing` | 0 to 0.5 | swing of this track, replacing the global one |
| `shift` | whole number, -1024 to 1024 | moves the pattern by steps of the first bar |
| `velocity` | 0 to 1 | how hard every note of the track plays |
| `glide` | 0 to 2 | seconds a legato note takes to slide to the next pitch |
| `inversion` | whole number, 0 to 3 | which chord note goes on top: 0 root position, 1 to 3 inversions |
| `arp-octaves` | whole number, 1 to 3 | how many octaves the arpeggio climbs |
| `delay` | one of 1/8, 3/16, and 1/4 | send 0.35 to the delay line of that division |
| `voicing` | one of close, open, spread, and drop2 | how a chord instrument spreads the notes of each chord |
| `arp` | one of up, down, updown, random, and played | plays a chord instrument's chords one note at a time, in this order |
| `arp-rate` | one of 1/4, 1/8, 3/16, 1/12, 1/16, 1/24, and 1/32 | the length of each arpeggio note, as a division of the bar |
| `lowpass` | 20 to 20,000, or a signal | low-pass filter cutoff, in Hz: lower is darker |
| `lowpass-q` | 0 to 1, or a signal | resonance of the low-pass filter |
| `highpass` | 20 to 20,000, or a signal | high-pass filter cutoff, in Hz: higher is thinner |
| `highpass-q` | 0 to 1, or a signal | resonance of the high-pass filter |
| `distort` | 0 to 1, or a signal | drive into a soft distortion |
| `crush` | 0 to 1, or a signal | bitcrush: fewer bits and a lower sample rate |
| `chorus` | 0 to 1, or a signal | chorus depth: a thicker, wider copy |
| `chorus-rate` | 0.05 to 5, or a signal | speed of the chorus, in Hz |
| `phaser` | 0 to 1, or a signal | phaser depth: a sweeping notch |
| `phaser-rate` | 0.05 to 5, or a signal | speed of the phaser, in Hz |
| `eq-low` | -18 to 18, or a signal | low shelf of the EQ, in dB |
| `eq-mid` | -18 to 18, or a signal | mid band of the EQ, in dB |
| `eq-mid-freq` | 200 to 8000, or a signal | centre of the EQ's mid band, in Hz |
| `eq-high` | -18 to 18, or a signal | high shelf of the EQ, in dB |
| `comp` | 0 to 1, or a signal | compressor amount: louder, more even |
| `gate` | 0 to 1, or a signal | gate amount: cuts the tail between notes |

`reverb` and `delay` send to shared buses: the reverb spaces named in the table and three delay lines. The spaces are presets of an algorithmic reverb, not recordings of places.

### Section modifiers

| Modifier | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tempo` | 40 to 300 | tempo from this section on |
| `gain` | 0 to 1 | volume of every track of the section |

### Values and signals

A value is a number, a name (`sea`), a division (`3/16`) or a signal with a range: `sine(8) 300..2400`. Signal shapes are `sine`, `tri`, `saw`, `square` and `rand`. The range is required and must fit the parameter; the period is above 0 and at most 256 bars. A signal restarts at the start of each section of a song.

### When changes play

A change to a constant number plays immediately. Every other change, structural, waits for the next bar not yet scheduled. In Song mode, a queued part and a mode switch wait for the next 4-bar phrase.

### Limits

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_SOURCE_LENGTH` | 65,536 | characters in a text |
| `MAX_NAME_LENGTH` | 24 | characters in a track or section name |
| `MAX_STEPS_PER_BAR` | 64 | steps in one bar |
| `MAX_BARS_PER_PATTERN` | 64 | bars in one pattern |
| `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` | 4 | nesting depth of [ ] groups |
| `MIN_REPEAT` | 1 | smallest *n repeat |
| `MAX_REPEAT` | 16 | largest *n repeat |
| `MAX_SHIFT` | 1024 | largest shift, in steps, either way |
| `MAX_TRANSPOSE` | 24 | largest transpose, in semitones, either way |
| `MIN_TEMPO` | 40 | lowest tempo, in BPM |
| `MAX_TEMPO` | 300 | highest tempo, in BPM |
| `DEFAULT_TEMPO` | 132 | tempo when the text has none |
| `MAX_SWING` | 0.5 | largest swing |
| `MAX_SIGNAL_PERIOD` | 256 | longest signal period, in bars |
| `MIN_PART_BARS` | 1 | shortest song part, in bars |
| `MAX_PART_BARS` | 256 | longest song part, in bars |
| `DEFAULT_PROBABILITY` | 0.5 | chance of ? without a number |
| `MIN_LOOP_BARS` | 1 | shortest loop <bars> |
| `MAX_LOOP_BARS` | 16 | longest loop <bars> |

### Grammar

The normative grammar is the Lezer grammar the app's parser is generated from. Keywords extend names, so `sine:` and `loop:` are still valid track names, and a track without a pattern parses and then fails with `EMPTY_PATTERN`.

```text

// Normative Lezer grammar of the Untzel language. The conformance test checks that
// the reference examples of the language analyze without errors.

@top Source { (Line? newline)* Line? }

Line { TitleStatement | TempoStatement | KeyStatement | SwingStatement | LoopStatement | Track | SectionDecl | SongDecl }

TitleStatement { kw<"title"> String }
TempoStatement { kw<"tempo"> Number }
KeyStatement { kw<"key"> Tonic Name }
SwingStatement { kw<"swing"> Number }
LoopStatement { kw<"loop"> Number }

Track { (TrackName ":")? InstrumentName Preset? Pattern? ("|" Modifier)* }

Preset { PresetName }
TrackName { Name }
InstrumentName { Name }

SectionDecl { kw<"section"> Name Name+ ("|" Modifier)* }
SongDecl { kw<"song"> Part ("," Part)* ("|" kw<"loop">)? }
Part { Name Number }

Pattern { Bar ("/" Bar)* }
Bar { Element+ }
Element { Atom Accent? Probability? Repeat? }

Accent { "!" }
Probability { "?" Number? }
Repeat { "*" Number }
Atom { Hits | Note | Stack | Chord | Sustain | Group }

Stack { Note ("+" Note)+ }
Group { "[" Element+ "]" }

Modifier { ModifierName Value? }
ModifierName { Name | kw<"swing"> | kw<"tempo"> }
Value { Number | Signal Range? | Division | Name }
Signal { SignalShape "(" (Number | Division) ")" }
SignalShape { kw<"sine"> | kw<"tri"> | kw<"saw"> | kw<"square"> | kw<"rand"> | kw<"env"> }
Range { Number ".." Number }
Division { Number "/" Number }

kw<term> { @extend[@name={term}]<Name, term> }

@skip { space | Comment }

@tokens {
  space { $[ \t]+ }
  newline { "\r"? "\n" }
  Comment { "//" ![\n]* }
  Number { "-"? @digit+ ("." @digit+)? }
  // The song title: one line, \" and \\ are the only escapes.
  String { '"' (![\\\n"] | "\\" $["\\])* '"' }
  Name { $[a-z] $[a-z0-9_\-]* }
  Hits { $[xX.] $[xX.~]* }
  Sustain { "~" }
  Note { $[a-g] $[b#]? @digit }
  Tonic { $[a-g] $[b#]? }
  // A preset never starts with "x" (a hit) nor reads like a note or a tonic.
  PresetName { $[h-wyz] $[a-z0-9\-]* | $[a-g] $[ac-z\-] $[a-z0-9\-]* | $[a-g] "b" $[a-z\-] $[a-z0-9\-]* }
  Chord { $[A-G] $[b#]? ("maj7" | "m7" | "m" | "7" | "sus2" | "sus4" | "dim" | "6" | "m6" | "9"
          | "m9" | "maj9" | "add9" | "madd9" | "aug" | "dim7" | "m7b5" | "7sus4" | "11" | "m11" | "13")? }
  @precedence { Comment, "/" }
  ":" "|" "," "/" "?" "*" "[" "]" "(" ")" ".." "!" "+"
}
```

### Errors

Analysis never throws: it returns the program or a list of diagnostics, each with a position, a stable code and a message, which the app shows in its language (the English text is the source). Syntax errors give one diagnostic per line. The codes are a stable contract; the messages may change. The messages below are the ones the app shows today in English; the Portuguese page shows the Portuguese ones.

| Code | Severity | Message | How to fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `UNKNOWN_INSTRUMENT` | error | Unknown instrument "kik". Did you mean "kick"? | Use one of the instruments on the Instruments page; the message suggests the closest name. |
| `DUPLICATE_TRACK_NAME` | error | A track named "bass" already exists on line 1. | Give each track its own name before the colon, for example bass2. |
| `UNKNOWN_TRACK` | error | Section "drop" uses "acid", but no track has that name. | List only track names that exist above the section, or add the missing track. |
| `UNKNOWN_SECTION` | error | The song uses "chorus", but no section has that name. | Use a section name declared with section, or declare it. |
| `DUPLICATE_SECTION_NAME` | error | A section named "drop" already exists on line 3. | Rename one of the sections; names are unique among sections. |
| `UNKNOWN_MODIFIER` | error | "bass" has no parameter "cutof". Did you mean "cutoff"? | Use a general modifier or a parameter of that instrument; the message suggests the closest one. |
| `OUT_OF_RANGE` | error | tempo must be between 40 and 300. | Bring the value inside the range the message gives. |
| `EMPTY_PATTERN` | error | This track has no steps. | Write at least one step after the instrument name, for example x... x... x... x... |
| `INVALID_NOTE` | error | "b9" is not a note. | Write a lower-case note with its octave, a to g, optional b or #, then a digit: c2, eb2, f#1. |
| `SIGNAL_NEEDS_RANGE` | error | sine(8) needs a range, for example 40..8000. | Follow the signal with a range inside the parameter's limits, for example 300..2400. |
| `SOURCE_TOO_LONG` | error | A song can have at most 65,536 characters. | Split the music or remove repeated lines: a text has a size limit. |
| `SYNTAX_ERROR` | error | Unexpected "]". | Check the line against the grammar: a stray bracket, bar or comma is the usual cause. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | error | Something went wrong while reading this text. | Not caused by your text. The last valid version keeps playing; reload the page if it repeats. |
| `UNKNOWN_SCALE` | error | Unknown scale "minr". Did you mean "minor"? | Use one of the scales listed in the reference; the message suggests the closest one. |
| `NAME_TOO_LONG` | error | A name can have at most 24 characters. | Shorten the track or section name. |
| `TOO_MANY_STEPS` | error | A bar can have at most 64 steps. | Use fewer steps in the bar, or groups in brackets to subdivide a step. |
| `TOO_MANY_BARS` | error | A pattern can have at most 64 bars. | Use fewer bars in the pattern, or sections and a song for longer music. |
| `PATTERN_KIND_MISMATCH` | error | "bass" plays notes, not chords. | Drums play hits (x . ~), pitched instruments play notes (c2). Check the instrument's kind. |
| `MISSING_VALUE` | error | gain needs a value, for example gain 0.8. | Give the modifier a value, as in the example the message shows. |
| `DUPLICATE_SONG` | error | A text can have only one song. | Keep one song line and join the parts with commas. |
| `OUT_OF_ORDER` | error | Sections come after tracks. | Order the text: tempo, key, swing and loop first, then tracks, then sections, then the song. |
| `DUPLICATE_STATEMENT` | error | tempo is already set on line 1. | Keep one title, one tempo, one key, one swing and one loop line; the first one counts. |
| `DUPLICATE_MODIFIER` | warning | gain is set twice; the last one wins. | A warning, not an error: remove the earlier copy; the last one wins. |
| `UNKNOWN_PRESET` | error | "piano" has no sound "brigth". Did you mean "bright"? | Use one of the instrument's sounds listed on the Instruments page; the message suggests the closest one. |
| `UNKNOWN_CHOICE` | error | "wave" can be saw, square, triangle or sine. | Use one of the names the message lists. |
| `SIGNAL_NEEDS_NUMBER` | error | "wave" takes a name, not a signal. | Write one of the parameter's names: a signal only moves numbers. |
| `NO_EFFECT` | warning | legato needs a one-voice instrument; "bass" plays several voices. | A warning, not an error: the modifier is ignored. Use it on the kind of instrument the message names, or add what it needs. |
| `TOO_MANY_MODULATORS` | error | A track can have at most 8 fast signals. | Give some parameters a slow signal (a period of 1 bar or more) or a fixed value; the message gives the limit per track. |
| `DUPLICATE_LOOP_SECTION` | error | Only one section can be the loop; "groove" already is on line 3. | Keep \| loop on one section only: it is the one loop mode plays. |
| `EMPTY_TITLE` | warning | The song title is empty; the last title stays. | A warning, not an error: write the name between the quotes, or remove the title line; the music keeps playing. |
| `TITLE_TOO_LONG` | warning | A song title can have at most 60 characters. | A warning, not an error: shorten the title to 60 characters; the first 60 are kept. |
| `SIGNAL_NOT_ALLOWED` | error | swing takes a number, not a signal. | Write a number: this value holds for the whole track or section. |
| `NOTHING_TO_PLAY` | warning | Nothing to play: add a track. | A warning, not an error: add a track. |

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/reference/

## Instruments

Every instrument of this build, generated from its manifest: the same file the analyzer, the track detail and the sound engine read. If it is not on this page, the app does not have it.

Each parameter is a modifier of the track: `| cutoff 900`. Its value can be a number inside the range or a signal ([Language guide](https://untzel.com/docs/en/language/#signals)). An exponential curve moves evenly through the octaves of the range, as an ear hears frequency and time. `tone` is the one-finger macro of a tile: from 0 to 1 it moves the parameters listed under each instrument between the two values shown. An explicit parameter in the text wins over `tone`.

Some instruments play recordings. On `piano`, `strings`, `harp`, `mallet`, `bell`, `kalimba` and `choir` the `source` parameter is `samples` by default, and `| source synth` plays the synthesized voice instead; on `vox`, the `ooh` and `aah` sounds play recorded singers. A recording is downloaded only when a track uses it, and until it arrives the synthesized voice plays, so the music never waits ([Credits](https://untzel.com/docs/en/credits/)). The model name next to each instrument is the name the library shows; the word you write in the text is always the one in the heading.

The kind decides what a pattern may contain: drums play hits (`x . ~`), pitched instruments play notes (`c2`), chord instruments play chords (`Cm7`).

Available now: Instrument library with search and preview. Nine categories, from drums to FX; search, preview a sound before adding it, and add the same instrument as often as you like.

### acid

Squelchy resonant mono bass

Model: NEON B3. Group: Bass. Kind: pitched: plays notes. Voices: 1. Default duck: 0.6.

#### Sounds

| Sound | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `classic` (default) | The classic squelch |
| `squelch` | More resonance and accent |
| `square` | Hollow square wave |
| `soft` | Round, a saw and a triangle in a 12 dB filter |

Default pattern: `acid: acid c2 c2 c3 c2 eb2 c2 bb1 c2`

| Parameter | Min | Max | Default | Unit | Curve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cutoff` | 40 | 12,000 | 700 | Hz | exponential |
| `resonance` | 0 | 1 | 0.6 | none | linear |
| `accent` | 0 | 1 | 0.6 | none | linear |
| `wave` | `saw` | `square` | `saw` | one of saw and square |  |
| `decay` | 0.05 | 2 | 0.25 | s | exponential |
| `wave2` | `saw` | `sine` | `saw` | one of saw, square, triangle, and sine |  |
| `mix` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |
| `sync` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |
| `filter` | `lp12` | `hp` | `lp24` | one of lp12, lp24, bp, and hp |  |
| `filter-attack` | 0.001 | 4 | 0.001 | s | exponential |
| `drive` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |
| `spread` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |
| `sub` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |
| `noise` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |

#### What tone moves

| Parameter | At tone 0 | At tone 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cutoff` | 150 | 6000 |
| `resonance` | 0.2 | 0.95 |

| `sub` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |
| `noise` | 0 | 1 | 0 | none | linear |

#### What tone moves

| Parameter | At tone 0 | At tone 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cutoff` | 400 | 9000 |
