## Cookbook

Recipes that play as they are, written only with the instruments of this build ([Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/)). Paste one into the Code panel, let it play, then change one thing at a time.

### A 124 BPM melodic groove

A steady kick, two hat layers and a sub, under a bass melody that walks through four chords of A minor, one per bar. The melody's filter opens and closes over 16 bars with `sine(16)`, and `delay 3/16` with `reverb wide` gives it space. `duck` makes the sub and the melody dip under every kick.

```untzel
// 124 BPM melodic groove in A minor: a bass melody over a steady kick
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.06

kick:   kick x... x... x... x...                     | decay 0.55 | drive 0.25 | pitch 46
hat:    hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                     | open 0.3 | color 0.6 | gain 0.5
ticks:  hat  x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.                     | decay 0.02 | gain 0.25 | pan 0.35
sub:    bass a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . g1 ~ . .     | cutoff 160 | duck 0.6
melody: bass a2 . c3 . e3 . c3 . / g2 . b2 . d3 . b2 . / f2 . a2 . c3 . a2 . / e2 . g2 . b2 . e3 . | cutoff sine(16) 500..2200 | decay 0.35 | delay 3/16 | reverb wide | gain 0.55 | duck 0.4
```

Try `swing 0.12` for a looser feel, or `pitch 42` on the kick for a deeper one.

### Rolling bass with duck

The bass plays three sixteenths after every kick and stays out of the kick's way with `duck 0.85`: the higher the value, the deeper it dips when the kick hits. A short `decay` keeps the notes tight.

```untzel
// rolling bass: off-beat sixteenths that dip under every kick
tempo 126
key f minor

kick: kick x... x... x... x...                                  | drive 0.3 | decay 0.4
roll: bass . f1 f1 f1 . f1 f1 f1 . f1 f1 f1 . f1 ab1 c2         | cutoff 650 | decay 0.12 | drive 0.35 | duck 0.85
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                                  | open 0.2 | gain 0.45
```

Try `cutoff 1200` for a brighter roll, or change the last three notes of the bar for a different turn.

### Percussion with swing and chance

The global `swing` shuffles every track; the shaker overrides it with its own `swing 0.2`. `x?0.3` on the ghost kick and `x?0.5` inside the shaker group play only some of the time, and `pan rand(2)` moves the shaker to a new place every two bars. The draws are deterministic: the same text always plays the same.

```untzel
// percussion: a swung shuffle where some hits only happen by chance
tempo 124
swing 0.14

kick:   kick x... x... x... x...
ghost:  kick . . . . . . x?0.3 . . . . . . . x?0.2 .   | gain 0.45 | decay 0.2 | pitch 60
hat:    hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                       | open 0.45 | color 0.7
shaker: hat  [x x?0.5]*8                               | decay 0.02 | gain 0.3 | swing 0.2 | pan rand(2) -0.4..0.4
```

Try raising a chance to `x?0.8`, or `[x x?0.5]*4` for a slower shaker.

### Builds with saw

In a song, a signal starts again at the start of each section, so `saw(4)` in a 4-bar section rises exactly from its first bar to its last. Here the hats open, the roll gets louder and the bass filter climbs until the drop, which starts the cycle again.

```untzel
// a 4-bar build: every saw(4) restarts with the section and rises exactly across it
tempo 126
key a minor

kick: kick x... x... x... x...                         | drive saw(4) 0.1..0.6
hat:  hat  x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.                         | open saw(4) 0..0.9 | gain saw(4) 0.3..0.7
roll: hat  x*4 x*4 x*4 x*4 / x*4 x*4 x*8 x*8           | decay 0.03 | gain saw(4) 0.1..0.8
bass: bass a1 . a1 . a1 . a1 . a1 . a1 . a1 . a1 .     | cutoff saw(4) 200..4000 | duck 0.5

section build kick hat roll bass
section drop  kick hat bass

song build 4, drop 8 | loop
```

Try `build 8` with `saw(8)` for a longer build.

### A whole song with sections

The groove of the first recipe as a song: an intro, a build, a drop, a break, another build and drop, and an outro. Sections choose which tracks play; the song decides how many bars each lasts. Switch the transport to `Song` to hear it from the start.

```untzel
// a whole song: intro, build, drop, break, build, drop, outro
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.05

kick:   kick x... x... x... x...                     | decay 0.5 | drive 0.25
hat:    hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                     | open 0.3 | gain 0.5
ticks:  hat  x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.                     | decay 0.02 | gain 0.25 | pan 0.3
roll:   hat  x*4 x*4 x*4 x*4                         | decay 0.03 | gain saw(4) 0.1..0.7
sub:    bass a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . g1 ~ . .     | cutoff 160 | duck 0.6
melody: bass a2 . c3 . e3 . c3 . / g2 . b2 . d3 . b2 . / f2 . a2 . c3 . a2 . / e2 . g2 . b2 . e3 . | cutoff sine(16) 500..2200 | decay 0.35 | delay 3/16 | reverb wide | gain 0.55 | duck 0.4

section intro kick hat ticks
section build kick hat ticks roll sub
section drop  kick hat ticks sub melody
section break ticks melody                           | gain 0.8
section outro kick ticks

song intro 8, build 4, drop 16, break 8, build 4, drop 16, outro 8
```

Try another order in the `song` line, or `| loop` at its end.

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/cookbook/

## Using AI

An assistant such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini can write Untzel code for you, if it knows the language first. The prompt below teaches it everything it needs: the syntax, the instruments of this build with every parameter and range, the limits and the errors. Then you ask for music in your own words and paste the answer into the app.

### How it works

1. Copy the prompt below and paste it at the start of a conversation with the assistant.
2. Ask for what you want to hear: a style, a tempo, a mood, a structure.
3. The assistant answers with one block of Untzel code. Copy only the code.
4. Paste it into the Code panel. It plays on the next bar.

The prompt is generated from the same sources as these pages, so it always lists the instruments and limits of this build. It is in English because the code is; the assistant answers in the language you write in. The same text is in [llms-full.txt](https://untzel.com/docs/llms-full.txt), for tools that read it directly.

### The prompt

### Example requests

Three requests and an answer that follows the prompt. Each answer plays as it is.

#### A melodic groove

"Write a 124 BPM loop in A minor, deep and hypnotic, with a bass melody."

```untzel
// deep melodic loop, 124 BPM, A minor
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.06

kick:   kick x... x... x... x...                       | decay 0.55 | drive 0.2 | pitch 45
hat:    hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                       | open 0.35 | color 0.55 | gain 0.5
shaker: hat  [x x?0.6]*8                               | decay 0.02 | gain 0.22 | pan rand(2) -0.3..0.3
sub:    bass a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . .       | cutoff 150 | duck 0.7
melody: bass e3 . a2 . c3 . e3 . / d3 . g2 . b2 . d3 . | cutoff sine(8) 600..2000 | decay 0.3 | delay 3/16 | reverb sea | gain 0.5 | duck 0.4
```

#### A build before the drop

"Add a 4-bar build before the drop that rolls the hats and opens the filter."

```untzel
// the loop with a 4-bar build before the drop
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.06

kick:   kick x... x... x... x...                       | decay 0.55 | drive 0.2 | pitch 45
hat:    hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                       | open 0.35 | color 0.55 | gain 0.5
shaker: hat  [x x?0.6]*8                               | decay 0.02 | gain 0.22 | pan rand(2) -0.3..0.3
sub:    bass a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . .       | cutoff 150 | duck 0.7
melody: bass e3 . a2 . c3 . e3 . / d3 . g2 . b2 . d3 . | cutoff sine(8) 600..2000 | decay 0.3 | delay 3/16 | reverb sea | gain 0.5 | duck 0.4
// build only: these rise across its 4 bars
roll:   hat  x*4 x*4 x*4 x*4                           | decay 0.03 | gain saw(4) 0.1..0.75
lift:   bass a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 .   | cutoff saw(4) 200..5000 | gain 0.4 | duck 0.5

section build kick hat roll lift sub
section drop  kick hat shaker sub melody

song build 4, drop 16 | loop
```

#### A whole song

"Turn it into a whole song of about three minutes, with an intro, two drops and a break."

```untzel
// a whole song of about three minutes: 92 bars at 124 BPM
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.06

kick:   kick x... x... x... x...                       | decay 0.55 | drive 0.2 | pitch 45
hat:    hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.                       | open 0.35 | color 0.55 | gain 0.5
shaker: hat  [x x?0.6]*8                               | decay 0.02 | gain 0.22 | pan rand(2) -0.3..0.3
sub:    bass a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . . a1 ~ . .       | cutoff 150 | duck 0.7
melody: bass e3 . a2 . c3 . e3 . / d3 . g2 . b2 . d3 . | cutoff sine(8) 600..2000 | decay 0.3 | delay 3/16 | reverb sea | gain 0.5 | duck 0.4
roll:   hat  x*4 x*4 x*4 x*4                           | decay 0.03 | gain saw(4) 0.1..0.75
lift:   bass a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 . a2 .   | cutoff saw(4) 200..5000 | gain 0.4 | duck 0.5
pad:    bass a2 ~ ~ ~ c3 ~ ~ ~ / g2 ~ ~ ~ b2 ~ ~ ~     | cutoff 900 | decay 1.5 | reverb sea | gain 0.35

section intro kick hat shaker
section build kick hat roll lift sub
section drop  kick hat shaker sub melody
section break shaker pad melody                        | gain 0.8
section outro kick shaker

song intro 16, build 4, drop 16, break 16, build 4, drop 24, outro 12
```

### Paste into the Code panel

Open **Code**, next to **Drop**, select all the text, and paste the answer over it. Copy only what is inside the code block: the lines before and after it are the assistant talking. When you stop typing the text is analyzed, and if it is valid it plays on the next bar. In Song mode the song starts from its first part.

### Reading the errors

If the answer has a mistake, the app underlines it and shows a code and a message, such as `UNKNOWN_MODIFIER` with `"bass" has no parameter "cutof". Did you mean "cutoff"?`. The previous version keeps playing. Copy the message back to the assistant and ask it to fix exactly that; the prompt teaches it every code. The [reference](https://untzel.com/docs/en/reference/#errors) lists every error with its fix.

### Good requests

- Say the tempo and the key, or ask the assistant to choose them.
- Name the parts you want: a loop, or a song with intro, build, drop, break.
- Ask for one change at a time once you like the music: "more swing on the hats", "a darker bass".
- Ask for instruments the app has. If you ask for one it does not have, the prompt tells the assistant to say so and use the closest one.

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/ai/

## For developers

How Untzel is built, for people who want to understand it, extend it or embed it. The design is documented and the source code is open.

### The source code

The source code is on GitHub at [technoinspire/untzel](https://github.com/technoinspire/untzel), under the license below. To contribute, read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/technoinspire/untzel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Contributor License Agreement](https://github.com/technoinspire/untzel/blob/main/CLA.md). This page describes the architecture, the instrument contract and the rules every contribution follows.

### Packages and the dependency rule

Untzel is a TypeScript monorepo with a Rust sound engine. Dependencies point inward only: the core knows nothing about the browser, Web Audio, the DOM or any interface library, and a tool checks the rule on every change.

| Layer | Packages | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| domain | `core`, `templates` | exact rational time, events, patterns, signals, scales, the program model, the instrument manifest contract; the template library by style |
| language | `language`, `commands` | grammar, analysis into a program, diagnostics, minimal text edits; the command line of the Code panel, which plans the same minimal edits |
| application | `transport`, `session` | scheduling ahead, bar-boundary changes, the song position and the play range; the use cases, the project library and their ports |
| adapters | `audio`, `dsp`, `visual`, `editor`, `controls`, `share`, `export` | Web Audio and the worker, the Rust DSP, the light, the code editor, the touch and keyboard controls; links, files and projects in the browser; the offline render of story, video and WAV |
| base | `i18n` | the one translation component, without DOM in its core |
| composition | the web app | the page at `app.untzel.com`, which wires everything |
| tools | `tools/sim`, `tools/docs`, `tools/release`, `tools/samples` | the simulator, these docs, the release package and the recorded instrument packs; never imported by the app |

The source text is the single source of truth of a session. Tiles, the song timeline and the editor are views that edit the same text; no gesture changes the music without going through it.

### Threads

| Thread | Runs | Talks through |
|---|---|---|
| main | interface, editor, controls, light rendering | a `MessagePort` to the worker |
| transport worker | the transport, querying the program 120 ms ahead | `MessagePort`s to the worklet and to the main thread |
| audio (`AudioWorklet`) | the DSP, compiled from Rust to WebAssembly with no imports, scheduling by sample | a `MessagePort` to the worker |

Sound is scheduled in the worker, so a main thread busy with typing or graphics does not delay it. Time is exact fractions, never floating point, so loops do not drift. The same events drive the sound and the light.

### The instrument contract

An instrument is a folder with a manifest and a voice:

```text
instruments/<name>/
  manifest.json   name, model, group, kind, engine, range, description, tags,
                  voices, allocation, steal, costPerVoice, patterns (name, text),
                  preview, defaultDuck, parameters (name, min, max, default, unit,
                  curve, or choices), tone mapping, toneLevelDb, presets,
                  defaultPreset, light
  voice.rs        implements the Voice trait of the DSP crate
  samples/v1/     pack.json and pack.opus, only for an instrument that plays recordings
  README.md       what it sounds like, parameters, credits
```

`patterns` holds one to six named starting patterns; the first is the one **Add track** writes, and the track detail offers them all. `model` is the name the library shows next to the language word, 3 to 20 letters, digits, spaces or hyphens, never a third party's brand. An instrument that plays recordings has a `source` parameter with the choices `synth` and `samples`, and its pack lists every source file it was built from.

The manifest is the only source of each parameter: the analyzer validates against it, the track detail draws a control for each parameter, and the [Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/) page is generated from it. A parameter cannot reuse a general modifier name, an exponential curve needs a minimum above 0, and every manifest is validated when the app is built.

### Local harness

Every change is verified locally before it is reported. The commands, for contributors:

```sh
pnpm check          # types, unit tests, Rust tests, layer rules, license headers, docs
pnpm check:full     # check, then production build, budgets, golden files, simulator, browser tests
pnpm sim song.untzel --bars 16    # the real language, transport and DSP in Node, to WAV
pnpm test:browser   # Playwright in the installed Chrome, with screenshots
pnpm docs:check     # rebuilds these docs and fails on any drift from the code
```

The simulator renders a text to WAV without a browser and fails on any NaN, clipping or kick drift.

### Releases

A version is published only by a tag: `vX.Y.Z`, a stable version on a commit that is already on the main branch. A merge publishes nothing. The tag runs the checks and the production build, then makes one package, `untzel-<version>.tar.gz`, with `app/` (the app), `docs/` (these pages) and, at its root, `LICENSE`, `ATTRIBUTION.md` and `TRADEMARKS.md`, which the license asks to travel with every copy. The package is deterministic: the same commit gives the same bytes. Next to it, `untzel-<version>.manifest.json` lists every file with its size and SHA-256. Each release is announced to the project's site, which serves the app at `app.untzel.com` and these docs at `untzel.com/docs/`; `untzel.com` is the site itself.

### Hosting a copy

The `app/` folder of a release is a static site. A copy you host yourself needs two things from the server. The first is the type `application/wasm` for the `.wasm` file: without it the sound engine loads by a slower path. The second is the app's Content-Security-Policy, the same on every response:

```text
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self' blob:; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'
```

It is static: no nonce, no hash and no `'unsafe-inline'`. The code editor builds its styles as constructed stylesheets, which the policy allows, so nothing in the page needs an inline style or script. The docs in `docs/` run under a stricter static policy of their own, with no WebAssembly, workers or `blob:`.

In return, every copy that runs for someone, including a fork, a modified or self-hosted copy and a page that embeds the player, must show the attribution: the Untzel logo, unmodified, at least 16 px high and linked to untzel.com, in the top bar; the line "Powered by Untzel · Techno Inspire", always on screen, in the footer; and the notice "Copyright (c) 2026 Techno Inspire", in the about or legal notice. Every exported video must end with the closing card of the Techno Inspire | Untzel logo and the address untzel.com. The attribution must stay legible and is never hidden, covered, cropped or made transparent. This is a condition of the license, not a request. The app itself goes further than the license asks: its videos also carry the logo and the address on every frame, and the closing card lasts 2 seconds ([Share and Export](https://untzel.com/docs/en/app/#share-export)). Third-party material the app bundles keeps its own license and credit ([Credits](https://untzel.com/docs/en/credits/)).

### Trademarks

"Untzel", "Techno Inspire", the Untzel logo and the Techno Inspire logo are trademarks of Techno Inspire, and the code license does not grant them beyond the attribution it requires. The model names of the instruments (AURA Grand, VOLTA K9 and the others on the [Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/) page) are Techno Inspire's names too and follow the same rules. Without asking, you may show the attribution, say truthfully that your project is based on or compatible with Untzel, and link to untzel.com. A fork keeps the attribution and takes its own name: "MyName, based on Untzel by Techno Inspire" is fine, "Untzel Pro" is not. Presenting a modified version as the official one, changing the logo, or using the names to advertise your own events or products needs written permission.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Chords | Available now | Chord names such as Cm7 need an instrument of kind chord. |

| Instrument presets | Available now | Named sounds per instrument, previewed and chosen in the library and in the track's detail. |
| Template library by style | Available now | A Style list on the waiting screen, in alphabetical order with the number of projects of each; every project can be changed completely. |
| Loop length in bars | Available now | loop <bars> sets how many bars one pass of loop mode lasts; the Length chip of the transport writes it. |
| Share as a link | Available now | The whole text in the link fragment; a file when it is too long. |
| Continue where you left off | Available now | Continue on the waiting screen opens the project you edited last on this device. |
| Remix this, when opening a link | Available now | A link opens with a notice and plays on the first tap. |
| Export: story, video and WAV | Available now | Rendered offline: a 9:16 story up to 1:00 (about 15 s of what is playing without a play range), a 16:9 video or WAV audio up to 10:00, from the play range, the loop or the song. The music keeps playing. |
| Recorded voices for vox and choir | Available now | The ooh and aah sounds of vox and choir play recorded singers from VocalSet (CC BY 4.0), loaded only when a track uses them. |
| Export in HD or 4K | Available now | HD and 4K from the first time the sheet opens; Render tests the device first and renders HD where it cannot take 4K. After that test, 4K shows only where it passed. |
| Commands under the code | Available now | A command line in the Code panel that makes the same minimal edits as the controls, with a preview before anything destructive. |
| Play range in Loop and Song | Available now | Choose the bars or parts that repeat, play one part alone, and export the same range. Never written into the text. |
| Projects on this device and the project menu | Available now | Every project saved in this browser one second after an edit, with open, rename, duplicate and delete with undo, all from one menu. |
| Song title | Available now | The title line names the song in the top bar, the browser tab, the files and the exported video. |
| Recorded piano, strings, harp, mallet, bell and kalimba | Available now | Recordings from Salamander Grand Piano (CC BY 3.0), VSCO 2 Community Edition and the Versilian Community Sample Library (CC0), downloaded only when a track uses them. |

## What exists today

Untzel is in development. This page says what this build has and what is designed but not built yet. The marks are not written by hand: each one comes from a check on the build itself, so they change on their own when a feature arrives.

### What a mark means

**Available now** means this build has the feature. **Planned** means it is designed, but this build does not have it: a button for it may be on screen and do nothing yet. Nothing on these pages is promised with a date.

### One release, two addresses

The app at `app.untzel.com` and these docs at `untzel.com/docs/` come from the same release, made from one version tag ([For developers](https://untzel.com/docs/en/developers/#releases)). The marks on this page therefore describe the app you open from its button.

### Instruments of this build

The [Instruments](https://untzel.com/docs/en/instruments/) page is generated from this build, so it lists exactly the instruments you can use today, and the [Cookbook](https://untzel.com/docs/en/cookbook/) and the AI prompt use only those.

Source: https://untzel.com/docs/en/status/

## Credits

Untzel's code is Techno Inspire's, under CPAL-1.0 ([For developers](https://untzel.com/docs/en/developers/#license)). Some material the app ships is not: it keeps its own license, and the credit that license asks for travels with every copy, here, in `THIRD_PARTY.md` and in `credits.json` of the repository. This page is generated from `credits.json`, so it lists exactly what this build bundles.

### What the app bundles

Untzel plays recordings in fifteen instruments. The recorded sounds of `choir` and the `ooh` and `aah` sounds of `vox` are sung vowels from VocalSet, cut into held notes, tuned to each zone of the keyboard and, for the choir, summed into small ensembles. `piano` plays the Salamander Grand Piano; `strings` and `harp` play VSCO 2 Community Edition; `mallet`, `bell`, `kalimba`, `conga`, `bongo`, `cowbell`, `woodblock`, `shaker`, `clap` and `hat` play the Versilian Community Sample Library. Each recording is downloaded only when a track uses it, and the instrument plays its synthesized voice until it arrives. Every other sound of Untzel is synthesized on your device. The interface uses two fonts, Hanken Grotesk and Jost, under the SIL Open Font License, with the license text bundled next to each.

### VocalSet: A Singing Voice Dataset

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Authors | Julia Wilkins, Prem Seetharaman, Alison Wahl, and Bryan Pardo |
| Performers | The 20 professional singers of VocalSet (anonymous: f1–f9, m1–m11) |
| License | Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International |
| Source | https://zenodo.org/records/1442513 |
| DOI | 10.5281/zenodo.1442513 |
| Used in | vox and choir |
| Changes made | Held notes cut from the straight long tones, moved to each zone root by pitch-synchronous overlap-add (and resampling past 7 semitones), summed into ensembles for the choir, band-limited to 16 kHz, levelled, looped with a baked crossfade and encoded as Opus. |

> Julia Wilkins, Prem Seetharaman, Alison Wahl and Bryan Pardo. VocalSet: A Singing Voice Dataset. In Proceedings of the 19th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR), Paris, 2018.

## Prompt

You write music in Untzel, the small text language of the Untzel app by Techno Inspire (https://app.untzel.com/). The person pastes your answer into the Code panel of the app, where it starts playing on the next bar.

### Rules
- Answer with exactly one fenced code block whose info string is untzel, then at most three short lines about what you wrote. Write those lines in the language the person uses; code, keywords, instrument names and parameter names stay in English.
- Write only the syntax on this page. Untzel is analyzed, never executed: it has no JavaScript, no functions, no variables, no imports, no for or while loops, no arithmetic and no expressions. Do not borrow syntax from Strudel, TidalCycles, Sonic Pi or any other tool.
- Use only these instruments: acid, bass, bell, bongo, boom, brass, choir, clap, conga, cowbell, crash, djembe, downlifter, epiano, fm-bass, fm-lead, harp, hat, impact, kalimba, kick, lead, mallet, noise, organ, pad, perc, piano, pluck, reese, ride, rim, riser, shaker, snare, square, stab, strings, sub, supersaw, sweep, tom, vox, woodblock. Use only the parameters listed for each, inside their ranges. If the person asks for an instrument that is not listed, say so and use the closest one listed.
- Every name is lower case: [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*, at most 24 characters. Comments start with // and run to the end of the line.

### Structure
A text has, in this order, each part optional:
1. globals, each at most once: title "<text>" (at most 60 characters, never changes the sound); tempo <bpm> (40..300, default 132); key <tonic> <scale> (tonic a..g with optional b or #; scales minor, major, dorian, phrygian, chromatic; default c minor); swing <amount> (0..0.5, default 0); loop <bars> (whole number 1..16; absent by default): in loop mode one pass lasts that many bars and every pattern restarts at its start, so a 4-bar pattern plays 4 times in loop 16; without it every pattern repeats on its own length. Song mode ignores it;
2. tracks, one per line: [<name>:] <instrument> <pattern> ( | <modifier> [value] )*. Two tracks may use the same instrument; each is its own instance;
3. sections: section <name> <track> <track> ... ( | tempo <bpm> ) ( | gain <0..1> );
4. at most one song: song <section> <bars>, <section> <bars> ... [ | loop ].
Without a song every track that is not muted plays in a loop. With sections and no song, each section plays 8 bars, in order, in a cycle.
```untzel
// globals first, then tracks, then sections, then the song
tempo 124
key a minor
swing 0.08

kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
bass: bass a1 . . a1 . . c2 .

section intro kick hat
section main  kick hat bass

song intro 8, main 16 | loop
```

### Patterns
- A pattern is one bar; / separates bars of a longer pattern, which repeats when it ends. The steps of a bar divide it equally.
- Hits for drum instruments: x hit, X accent, . rest, ~ holds the previous step one more step. In a run of hits every character is a step, so x... x... is 8 steps.
- [ ] subdivides one step; ? plays with a chance (default 0.5), as in x?0.3; *n repeats inside the same step, as in x*4.
```untzel
kick:  kick X... x... X... x...
clap:  hat  .... x~.. .... x~..   | open 0.4
roll:  hat  x x [x x] x*2         | decay 0.03
ghost: hat  x?0.3 x? x? x?        | gain 0.5
fill:  kick x... x... x... x... / x... x... x.x. xxxx
```

### Notes and the scale lock
- Pitched instruments play notes: lower-case letter, optional b or #, octave digit: c1, eb2, f#1. . is a rest and ~ holds the note.
- With a key, notes outside the scale move to the nearest degree of it; | free turns that off for one track, and key c chromatic turns it off everywhere.
- Chord names (Cm7, Abmaj7) need an instrument of kind chord; none of the listed instruments is one, so write notes.
```untzel
key c minor

sub:  bass c1 ~ . c1 ~ . c1 .         | cutoff 180
line: bass c2 eb2 g2 bb2 c3 . g2 .    | cutoff 1200 | decay 0.2
```

### General modifiers (every instrument)
Chained with |, read left to right; when one repeats, the last wins (warning DUPLICATE_MODIFIER). A change to a constant number sounds immediately; everything else enters on the next bar.
- mute (no value): silences the track
- free (no value): turns the scale lock off for this track
- legato (no value): one-voice instruments glide from note to note without a new attack
- gain 0..2, or a signal: volume
- pan -1..1, or a signal: position in the stereo field, left to right
- duck 0..1, or a signal: how much the track dips when the kick plays (sidechain)
- tone 0..1, or a signal: one-finger timbre macro: moves the parameters the instrument maps to it
- reverb small | wide | sea | room | plate | hall | dub | 0..1: send to a reverb space by name (send 0.3), or a send amount to wide
- transpose whole number -24..24: semitones, still under the scale lock
- swing 0..0.5: swing of this track, replacing the global one
- shift whole number -1024..1024: moves the pattern by steps of the first bar
- velocity 0..1: how hard every note of the track plays
- glide 0..2: seconds a legato note takes to slide to the next pitch
- inversion whole number 0..3: which chord note goes on top: 0 root position, 1 to 3 inversions
- arp-octaves whole number 1..3: how many octaves the arpeggio climbs
- delay 1/8 | 3/16 | 1/4: send 0.35 to the delay line of that division
- voicing close | open | spread | drop2: how a chord instrument spreads the notes of each chord
- arp up | down | updown | random | played: plays a chord instrument's chords one note at a time, in this order
- arp-rate 1/4 | 1/8 | 3/16 | 1/12 | 1/16 | 1/24 | 1/32: the length of each arpeggio note, as a division of the bar
- lowpass 20..20,000, or a signal: low-pass filter cutoff, in Hz: lower is darker
- lowpass-q 0..1, or a signal: resonance of the low-pass filter
- highpass 20..20,000, or a signal: high-pass filter cutoff, in Hz: higher is thinner
- highpass-q 0..1, or a signal: resonance of the high-pass filter
- distort 0..1, or a signal: drive into a soft distortion
- crush 0..1, or a signal: bitcrush: fewer bits and a lower sample rate
- chorus 0..1, or a signal: chorus depth: a thicker, wider copy
- chorus-rate 0.05..5, or a signal: speed of the chorus, in Hz
- phaser 0..1, or a signal: phaser depth: a sweeping notch
- phaser-rate 0.05..5, or a signal: speed of the phaser, in Hz
- eq-low -18..18, or a signal: low shelf of the EQ, in dB
- eq-mid -18..18, or a signal: mid band of the EQ, in dB
- eq-mid-freq 200..8000, or a signal: centre of the EQ's mid band, in Hz
- eq-high -18..18, or a signal: high shelf of the EQ, in dB
- comp 0..1, or a signal: compressor amount: louder, more even
- gate 0..1, or a signal: gate amount: cuts the tail between notes

### Signals
Every numeric parameter that allows it takes a slow wave instead of a number: <shape>(<bars>) <from>..<to>. Shapes: sine, tri, saw, square, rand, env. The range is required and stays inside the parameter's limits. The period is above 0 and at most 256 bars. In a song, a signal restarts at the start of every section, so saw(4) in a 4-bar section rises exactly across it.
```untzel
bass: bass c2 . c2 . c2 . eb2 .   | cutoff sine(8) 300..2400
hat:  hat  x.x. x.x. x.x. x.x.    | open tri(4) 0..0.8 | pan rand(1) -0.5..0.5
rise: hat  x x x x x x x x        | gain saw(4) 0.1..0.8
gate: hat  x*4 x*4 x*4 x*4        | gain square(2) 0.2..0.6
```

### Sections and song
```untzel
tempo 124
key a minor

kick: kick x... x... x... x...
hat:  hat  ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
sub:  bass a1 . . a1 . . a1 .     | cutoff 180
bass: bass . a2 . a2 . c3 . e2    | cutoff saw(4) 300..1800

section intro kick hat
section build kick hat sub bass   | gain 0.8
section drop  kick hat sub bass   | tempo 126

song intro 8, build 4, drop 16, intro 4
```

### Instruments
Per instrument: its group and kind (drum plays hits, pitched plays notes, chord plays chords); each parameter as name min..max=default unit, or name=default when it runs 0..1, or name choice|choice=default; what tone moves; its sounds, the default first (write a sound's name right after the instrument's name); its default pattern.
- acid: Bass, pitched. Parameters: cutoff 40..12,000=700 Hz; resonance=0.6; accent=0.6; wave saw|square=saw; decay 0.05..2=0.25 s; wave2 saw|square|triangle|sine=saw; mix=0; sync=0; filter lp12|lp24|bp|hp=lp24; filter-attack 0.001..4=0.001 s; drive=0; spread=0; sub=0; noise=0. tone: cutoff 150→6000, resonance 0.2→0.95. Sounds: classic, squelch, square, soft. Pattern: c2 c2 c3 c2 eb2 c2 bb1 c2
- bass: Bass, pitched. Parameters: cutoff 40..8000=600 Hz; decay 0.05..2=0.3 s; drive=0.1. tone: cutoff 120→3000. Sounds: round, bright, dirty, rolling. Pattern: c2 . . c2 . . c2 .
- bell: Plucks, chord. Parameters: brightness=0.5; feedback=0.1; decay 0.1..8=3 s; release 0.01..8=1.5 s. tone: brightness 0→1. Sounds: tubular, glass, toy. Pattern: c4 ~ ~ ~ g4 ~ ~ ~
- bongo: Drums, drum. Parameters: tune=0.6; decay 0.05..1=0.18 s; hardness=0.6; slap=0. tone: tune 0→1. Sounds: high, low, slap. Pattern: x.x. .x.x x.x. .xx.
- boom: Bass, pitched. Parameters: decay 0.1..8=1.2 s; tune=0.5; bend=0.3; color=0.45. tone: decay 0.3→4. Sounds: long, short, dirty. Pattern: c2 ~ ~ . . . c2 . / . . eb2 ~ ~ ~ . .
- brass: Brass, chord. Parameters: cutoff 200..12,000=700 Hz; contour=0.85; attack 0.001..2=0.04 s; release 0.01..4=0.2 s; detune=0.2; wave2 saw|square|triangle|sine=square; mix=0.25; sync=0; filter lp12|lp24|bp|hp=lp12; filter-attack 0.001..4=0.08 s; filter-decay 0.01..8=0.6 s; drive=0.5; spread=0; sub=0; noise=0.06; scoop=0.6. tone: cutoff 400→8000, contour 0→1. Sounds: section, soft, horn. Pattern: Cm ~ ~ ~
- choir: Voices, chord. Parameters: vowel=0; breath=0.25; brightness=0.5; attack 0.01..8=0.5 s; release 0.01..8=1 s; detune=0.4. tone: vowel 0→1, brightness 0→1. Sounds: aah, ooh, dark, chant, gospel, ethereal, monk. Pattern: Cm ~ ~ ~
- clap: Drums, drum. Parameters: decay 0.05..1=0.18 s; spread=0.4; color=0.5. tone: decay 0.08→0.6, spread 0.1→0.9. Sounds: tight, roomy, snap. Pattern: .... x... .... x...
- conga: Drums, drum. Parameters: tune=0.5; decay 0.05..2=0.3 s; bend=0.1; hardness=0.5; slap=0. tone: tune 0→1. Sounds: open, slap, muted, low, high. Pattern: ..x. x..x ..x. x.x.
- cowbell: Drums, drum. Parameters: tune=0.5; decay 0.02..1=0.22 s. tone: tune 0→1. Sounds: classic, bright. Pattern: ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
- crash: Drums, drum. Parameters: decay 0.2..8=1.8 s; color=0.5; size=0.6. tone: color 0→1. Sounds: wide, short. Pattern: x... .... .... ....
- djembe: Drums, drum. Parameters: tune=0.45; decay 0.05..2=0.35 s; bend=0.05; hardness=0.55; slap=0.25. tone: tune 0→1. Sounds: tone, bass, slap. Pattern: x..x ..x. x.x. ..x.
- downlifter: FX, drum. Parameters: length 0..30=0 s; cutoff 200..16,000=8000 Hz; resonance=0.4; color=0.5. tone: color 0→1. Sounds: noise, tone, both. Pattern: x~~~ ~~~~ ~~~~ ~~~~
- epiano: Keys, chord. Parameters: brightness=0.55; decay 0.1..8=2 s; release 0.01..8=0.4 s; detune=0.3; tine=0.7; tremolo=0.4. tone: brightness 0→1. Sounds: tine, bell, soft, bark. Pattern: Cm7 ~ ~ ~
- fm-bass: Bass, pitched. Parameters: brightness=0.45; feedback=0.4; decay 0.05..4=0.35 s; release 0.01..2=0.1 s. tone: brightness 0→1. Sounds: pluck, metal, round. Pattern: c2 . c2 . eb2 . c2 g1
- fm-lead: Leads, pitched. Parameters: brightness=0.5; feedback=0.2; attack 0.001..2=0.01 s; release 0.01..4=0.25 s. tone: brightness 0→1. Sounds: bright, brass, flute. Pattern: c4 ~ eb4 . g4 ~ ~ .
- harp: Plucks, chord. Parameters: brightness=0.5; decay 0.1..20=4 s; position=0.4; detune=0.3; release 0.01..4=0.6 s. tone: brightness 0→1. Sounds: concert, soft, glass. Pattern: c3 g3 eb4 g3
- hat: Drums, drum. Parameters: open=0; decay 0.01..0.5=0.06 s; color=0.5; band=0. tone: open 0→1. Sounds: closed, open, tight, dusty, metal. Pattern: ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
- impact: FX, drum. Parameters: decay 0.1..4=3.2 s; size=0.5; color=0.1; tail=0.6. tone: size 0→1. Sounds: hit, deep, metal. Pattern: x... .... .... ....
- kalimba: Plucks, chord. Parameters: hardness=0.6; brightness=0.5; decay 0.1..6=1.1 s; body=0.4; noise=0. tone: brightness 0→1. Sounds: tine, bright, soft, box. Pattern: c4 . eb4 . g4 . bb4 . / g4 . eb4 . c5 . g4 .
- kick: Drums, drum. Parameters: decay 0.05..1.5=0.45 s; drive=0.2; pitch 30..80=48 Hz; click=0.3; sweep 0..6=3.5; sweep-time 0.005..0.2=0.025 s; overtone=0; click-tone 100..8000=1500 Hz; grit=0. tone: decay 0.15→0.9, drive 0→0.7. Sounds: punch, tight, boom, hard, deep, warm, sharp, bright, rumble, dark, crisp, round. Pattern: x... x... x... x...
- lead: Leads, pitched. ### Limits
- characters in a text: 65,536
- characters in a track or section name: 24
- steps in one bar: 64
- bars in one pattern: 64
- nesting depth of [ ] groups: 4
- smallest *n repeat: 1
- largest *n repeat: 16
- largest shift, in steps, either way: 1024
- largest transpose, in semitones, either way: 24
- lowest tempo, in BPM: 40
- highest tempo, in BPM: 300
- tempo when the text has none: 132
- largest swing: 0.5
- longest signal period, in bars: 256
- shortest song part, in bars: 1
- longest song part, in bars: 256
- chance of ? without a number: 0.5
- shortest loop <bars>: 1
- longest loop <bars>: 16

### Errors
Invalid text never stops the music: the app keeps playing the last valid version and shows the code and message. If the person pastes an error back, fix exactly what it names.
- UNKNOWN_INSTRUMENT: Unknown instrument "kik". Did you mean "kick"? Use one of the instruments on the Instruments page; the message suggests the closest name.
- DUPLICATE_TRACK_NAME: A track named "bass" already exists on line 1. Give each track its own name before the colon, for example bass2.
- UNKNOWN_TRACK: Section "drop" uses "acid", but no track has that name. List only track names that exist above the section, or add the missing track.
- UNKNOWN_SECTION: The song uses "chorus", but no section has that name. Use a section name declared with section, or declare it.
- DUPLICATE_SECTION_NAME: A section named "drop" already exists on line 3. Rename one of the sections; names are unique among sections.
- UNKNOWN_MODIFIER: "bass" has no parameter "cutof". Did you mean "cutoff"? Use a general modifier or a parameter of that instrument; the message suggests the closest one.
- OUT_OF_RANGE: tempo must be between 40 and 300. Bring the value inside the range the message gives.
- EMPTY_PATTERN: This track has no steps. Write at least one step after the instrument name, for example x... x... x... x...
- INVALID_NOTE: "b9" is not a note. Write a lower-case note with its octave, a to g, optional b or #, then a digit: c2, eb2, f#1.
- SIGNAL_NEEDS_RANGE: sine(8) needs a range, for example 40..8000. Follow the signal with a range inside the parameter's limits, for example 300..2400.
- SOURCE_TOO_LONG: A song can have at most 65,536 characters. Split the music or remove repeated lines: a text has a size limit.
- SYNTAX_ERROR: Unexpected "]". Check the line against the grammar: a stray bracket, bar or comma is the usual cause.
- INTERNAL_ERROR: Something went wrong while reading this text. Not caused by your text. The last valid version keeps playing; reload the page if it repeats.
- UNKNOWN_SCALE: Unknown scale "minr". Did you mean "minor"? Use one of the scales listed in the reference; the message suggests the closest one.
- NAME_TOO_LONG: A name can have at most 24 characters. Shorten the track or section name.
- TOO_MANY_STEPS: A bar can have at most 64 steps. Use fewer steps in the bar, or groups in brackets to subdivide a step.
- TOO_MANY_BARS: A pattern can have at most 64 bars. Use fewer bars in the pattern, or sections and a song for longer music.
- PATTERN_KIND_MISMATCH: "bass" plays notes, not chords. Drums play hits (x . ~), pitched instruments play notes (c2). Check the instrument's kind.
- MISSING_VALUE: gain needs a value, for example gain 0.8. Give the modifier a value, as in the example the message shows.
- DUPLICATE_SONG: A text can have only one song. Keep one song line and join the parts with commas.
- OUT_OF_ORDER: Sections come after tracks. Order the text: tempo, key, swing and loop first, then tracks, then sections, then the song.
- DUPLICATE_STATEMENT: tempo is already set on line 1. Keep one title, one tempo, one key, one swing and one loop line; the first one counts.
- DUPLICATE_MODIFIER: gain is set twice; the last one wins. A warning, not an error: remove the earlier copy; the last one wins.
- UNKNOWN_PRESET: "piano" has no sound "brigth". Did you mean "bright"? Use one of the instrument's sounds listed on the Instruments page; the message suggests the closest one.
- UNKNOWN_CHOICE: "wave" can be saw, square, triangle or sine. Use one of the names the message lists.
- SIGNAL_NEEDS_NUMBER: "wave" takes a name, not a signal. Write one of the parameter's names: a signal only moves numbers.
- NO_EFFECT: legato needs a one-voice instrument; "bass" plays several voices. A warning, not an error: the modifier is ignored. Use it on the kind of instrument the message names, or add what it needs.
- TOO_MANY_MODULATORS: A track can have at most 8 fast signals. Give some parameters a slow signal (a period of 1 bar or more) or a fixed value; the message gives the limit per track.
- DUPLICATE_LOOP_SECTION: Only one section can be the loop; "groove" already is on line 3. Keep | loop on one section only: it is the one loop mode plays.
- EMPTY_TITLE: The song title is empty; the last title stays. A warning, not an error: write the name between the quotes, or remove the title line; the music keeps playing.
- TITLE_TOO_LONG: A song title can have at most 60 characters. A warning, not an error: shorten the title to 60 characters; the first 60 are kept.
- SIGNAL_NOT_ALLOWED: swing takes a number, not a signal. Write a number: this value holds for the whole track or section.
- NOTHING_TO_PLAY: Nothing to play: add a track. A warning, not an error: add a track.
Examples of common mistakes:
UNKNOWN_MODIFIER:
```untzel
bass: bass c2 . c2 . | cutof 400
```
SIGNAL_NEEDS_RANGE:
```untzel
bass: bass c2 . c2 . | cutoff sine(8)
```
PATTERN_KIND_MISMATCH:
```untzel
pad: bass Cm7 ~ ~ ~ / Abmaj7 ~ ~ ~
```
OUT_OF_ORDER:
```untzel
kick: kick x... x... x... x...
section drop kick
hat: hat ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.
```

### Answer
Start with tempo and key and give every track a name. Add sections and a song only when the person asks for a whole song with parts; otherwise write a loop.
